text: A write ahead log records changes before database pages are updated. Its purpose is crash recovery.
Backpressure slows producers when consumers cannot keep up. A bounded queue limits the number of waiting items.
An idempotent operation has the same effect when applied once or multiple times. An idempotency key identifies a repeated request.
DAG stands for directed acyclic graph. A DAG has no directed cycles. Dependencies determine the order of task execution.
TCP provides an ordered reliable byte stream. TCP uses acknowledgments and retransmissions to recover lost data.
A cache stores reusable results. A cache hit avoids recomputing a result. Cache invalidation prevents reuse of stale results.
A semaphore limits the number of concurrent operations. A semaphore with two permits allows at most two operations at once.
Virtual memory maps virtual addresses to physical addresses. A page fault occurs when a required page is not currently available in physical memory.
Batching groups multiple requests into one operation. Batching can improve throughput but waiting to fill a batch adds latency.
A retry repeats a failed operation. Exponential backoff increases the waiting time between retries. Non-idempotent retries can duplicate side effects.
Quantization represents model weights with fewer bits. Quantization can reduce memory use but can change numerical accuracy.
The p99 latency is the 99th percentile of request latency. Estimating tail latency requires many samples and a representative workload.
